inputs.sbc_source: 20-F FY2026 consolidated cash flow statement, share-based compensation expense (WIT_20F_FY2026.txt:10860), cross-checked to Note 25 (line 13756). No cash tax on net-share settlement exists: awards are satisfied through a controlled trust, EquityAwardTaxes kpi is 0 every year.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 (year to 31-Mar-2026) financing outflow for buybacks was nil. The Rs150,000m buyback of 600,000,000 shares at Rs250 (plus Rs497m costs) settled in Q1 FY2027 (WIT_6K_Q1-FY2027.txt:256-260, 340) and is reflected in BOTH the 30-Jun-2026 share count and the 30-Jun-2026 net cash used here. Wipro is a serial repurchaser (Rs145bn FY2024, Rs117bn FY2021, Rs105bn FY2020): the flat share count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in INR; NYSE ADS quote in USD, 1 ADS = 1 ordinary share (no ADS-ratio multiplier). fx_rate 0.010384 USD per INR = 1/96.30 (Yahoo INR=X regularMarketPrice 96.30, 2026-10-04). Parity check: WIPRO.NS Rs159.35 at the 2026-10-01 NSE close (Yahoo WIPRO.NS; 2-Oct was an NSE holiday) / 96.30 = USD 1.655 vs the USD 1.72 ADS close, a 4% ADS premium -- within Wipro's normal ADS premium range, confirms rate direction and quote basis. refresh_price.py moves the price but not the rate; re-derive the rate at each refresh.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z regular close (NYSE), Friday; not an after-hours print
inputs.share_count_basis: 9,903,549,797 shares issued at 30-Jun-2026 (WIT_6K_Q1-FY2027.txt:260, post the 600m-share buyback) less ~11.9m treasury shares held by the controlled trust plus ~16m dilutive options (diluted less basic weighted average, Q1 FY2027, lines 1525-1527) = ~9,908m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count. The Metrics.csv FY2026 figure (10,503m) is the FY2026 weighted-average diluted count and predates the June-2026 buyback; using it would overstate the count by 6%.
inputs.net_cash_note: 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet (WIT_6K_Q1-FY2027.txt:50-51, 82, 1000-1008): cash Rs88,444m + current investments (liquid mutual funds, FMPs, bonds, deposits) Rs307,281m = Rs395,725m; loans, borrowings and overdrafts Rs177,649m (all current, bank borrowings used as a cheap INR/USD funding leg against the investment book). Net cash Rs218,076m, down from Rs375,361m at 31-Mar-2026 after the Rs150.5bn buyback, the Rs33.0bn Mindsprint acquisition and Rs2.9bn purchase of NCI shares in the June quarter. Lease liabilities (Rs35,173m) are EXCLUDED from net debt because leases are charged in the flows (treatment B). Non-current investments Rs29,181m are added separately in equity_bridge; NCI book Rs2,059m deducted there.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income Rs28,367m (FY2026, Note 27, line 13578) plus FVTPL investment gains Rs7,763m are returns on the Rs396bn cash-and-investments pile that is added to EV in the bridge. Under Wipro's IFRS cash-flow presentation 'finance and other income, net of finance expenses' is reversed out of operating profit (line 10863) and interest received Rs28,878m is classified in INVESTING activities (line 10886), so reported OCF and therefore reported_fcf already exclude every rupee of investment income. interest_income is set to 0 to avoid deducting it a second time; the double-count the rule guards against cannot arise here. (Taxes paid in OCF do include tax on that income, ~Rs8.6bn/yr, a small conservatism left in place.)
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease cash payment (principal + interest, one line in financing: Rs11,561m FY2026, line 10893; Rs10,474m FY2025; Rs10,060m FY2024) deducted inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path (1.25% of revenue), and lease liabilities (Rs35,173m) EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for cash tax is therefore ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2026 D&A Rs29,107m = PPE depreciation 14,595 + ROU depreciation 6,725 + intangible amortisation 7,787 (lines 11644, 11697, 11813); da_pct_path starts from (14,595+7,787)/926,240 = 2.42%. Capex (Rs15,603m, 1.68%) is PPE only, consistent with the lease line funding ROU-asset renewal.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; NCI is immaterial (Rs43m of Rs33,563m Q1 FY2027 profit, Rs2,059m book at 30-Jun-2026). Charged ONCE, in the bridge, at book. Not folded into the tax/leakage driver.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR, the currency of the flows. India 10-year G-sec ~6.6% (Sep/Oct 2026, 6.3-6.8% range through FY2026) + beta 0.9 x INR equity risk premium ~5.5% = cost of equity ~11.5%. Gross debt is a funding leg fully covered by the investment book (net cash), so WACC = cost of equity = 11.5%, applied identically to all three scenarios (risk is charged once, in the probability-weighted flows). Cross-check: a USD WACC of ~9% for a mature IT-services major plus the ~2.5pp INR-USD risk-free differential lands in the same place, and the Gordon multiple at 11.5%/3.5% (12.9x FCF) sits just above Wipro's current ~11.5x EV/owner-FCF.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US'), with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied: (a) INR flows, INR WACC, USD quote via fx_rate; (b) lease treatment B; (c) NCI once, in the bridge; (d) excluded investment income matched by the cash+investments pile and non-current investments in the bridge; SBC is non-zero (0.48% of revenue) so house and street differ slightly. Fresh build, no prior DCF (memory has no WIT entry). FY0 = FY2026 (year to 31-Mar-2026) flows; balance sheet and share count are the LATER 30-Jun-2026 figures so that the Rs150bn June buyback is captured in both the count and the cash. The ~Rs26bn of owner FCF generated in Q1 FY2027 (Apr-Jun 2026) is therefore in the June cash AND inside the modelled FY2027 flow; this overlap is ~Rs2.6/share (~1.5% of value) and is left as is rather than hacking the flow. EBITDA margins in the driver paths are PRE-SBC (SBC is deducted separately by the engine): FY2026 pre-SBC EBITDA = 180,358 + 4,465 = 184,823 = 19.95%; Q1 FY2027 = (39,206 + 8,044 + 601)/244,786 = 19.55%. Cash tax: FY2026 taxes paid Rs26,245m were only ~17.6% of lease-adjusted EBIT against a 23.5% book effective rate; the gap accumulates in disputed/deferred tax liabilities (Rs102bn current+non-current tax liabilities) and is NOT perpetuated -- the model charges 24% rising to 25% as SEZ benefits sunset and Pillar Two bites. Owner FCF FY2026 = reported 133,713 - SBC 4,465 - lease payments 11,561 = 117,687 (12.7% of revenue); interest income already excluded by IFRS classification (see interest_income_note). Revenue growth is modelled in INR: Wipro's USD IT-services revenue has been flat for three years (FY2024 -0.8%, FY2025 -0.7%, FY2026 -0.3%) and INR growth comes from INR depreciation (~3%/yr long run, ~12% in the last 12 months) plus acquisitions (Mindsprint closed Jun-2026, ~USD 150m/yr). Q1 FY2027 INR revenue was +10.6% YoY on flat USD revenue; the FY2027 base growth of 7.0% is BELOW the FX-inflated run-rate, and later years fade to 3-3.5% INR, i.e. roughly zero to +1% real USD growth, which is what a company that has not grown in USD for three years has earned. The current margin trough (Q1 FY2027 IT-services margin ~16%, 15-quarter low) is not extrapolated: base recovers the pre-SBC EBITDA margin from 19.3% to 19.6% over two years and holds, which is still below the FY2026 actual.

equity_bridge.item: Non-current investments at book (FVTOCI equities, longer-dated bonds/FMPs)
equity_bridge.note: WIT_6K_Q1-FY2027.txt:37, 30-Jun-2026. Their income (dividends Rs3m, FVTOCI gains) is excluded from the flows, so the asset belongs in the bridge (matching-asset rule). Equity-method investees (Rs2,119m) deliberately omitted.
WIT_6K_Q1-FY2027.txt:68. Flows are consolidated; NCI charged once, here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle INR revenue growth, bracketed by revenue_3yr_cagr (0.8%, three flat USD years) and eps_3yr_cagr (6.7%, buyback-assisted); equity CAGR is distorted by Rs145bn FY2024 and Rs150bn FY2027 buybacks and the FY2022 Capco acquisition inflates every 5-year figure
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: equity_3yr_cagr 4.3% vs revenue_3yr_cagr 0.8%: equity has compounded faster than revenue because earnings were retained between buyback years (net income flat-to-up on flat revenue, EPS up on count reduction). The 5-year revenue CAGR of 8.4% is NOT organic: FY2022 included the Capco acquisition (+27.7% INR revenue that year) and ~3%/yr INR depreciation. Owner-FCF 5-year CAGR of 0.1% confirms the business has not grown its cash generation in five years.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - lease payments; interest income already excluded by IFRS classification): FY2021 117,003; FY2022 76,804; FY2023 102,087; FY2024 150,062; FY2025 138,664; FY2026 117,687 (Rs m). Owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are within 0.1-0.8pp of each other because SBC is tiny (0.5% of revenue) and lease cost is stable (1.1-1.3%); SBC is not eating the growth here. FY2024 owner FCF (150bn) was a working-capital release year (receivables fell on falling revenue) and FY2026 (118bn) a working-capital build year (+Rs14bn consumed on +Rs35bn revenue); the FY2024-FY2026 average of 135bn is the better mid-cycle anchor and the component build lands near it.

base.narrative: FY2027 +7.0% INR: flat USD organic revenue (Q2 FY2027 guide -1.5% to +0.5% cc QoQ), ~USD150m Mindsprint consolidation and the INR depreciation already in the Q1 run-rate; this is below the +10.6% Q1 print. Then 4.5% fading to 3.0% INR, i.e. 0-1% real USD growth with large-deal ramps (FY2026 TCV USD7.8bn, +45%) offsetting AI-driven deflation on renewals. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin recovers from the Q1 FY2027 trough (19.55%) only to 19.6%, below the FY2026 19.95%, as wage inflation and pre-growth investment are only partly offset by pyramid/automation gains. D&A drifts down as Capco/Rizing/Mindsprint intangibles amortise off; capex steady at 1.7%; growth consumes 15% of incremental revenue in receivables and unbilled work (FY2026 consumed 39%, FY2024-25 released on falling revenue). Cash tax 24% -> 25%, not the 17.6% actually paid in FY2026.

bull.narrative: The booking-to-revenue lag closes: the USD7.8bn FY2026 large-deal TCV and the Olam/Mindsprint USD800m committed spend ramp into 3-4% USD organic growth from FY2028, the consulting-led/AI-native pivot wins share in AI advisory and agentic-platform work rather than only losing it on commoditised ADM, and discretionary BFSI spend recovers with rates. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin climbs to 21% (IT-services margin ~18%, still below TCS/Infosys) on pyramid optimisation and AI delivery leverage. Terminal INR growth 4.0% (~1.5% USD).

bear.narrative: AI-assisted development (~25% coding-cost reduction) is passed to clients at every renewal: USD revenue declines 2-3% a year through FY2030 as contract values shrink faster than new large deals ramp, so INR growth is only the currency (FY2027 5.0% then 1-2%). Wage inflation and sub-contracting to fill AI skills gaps cannot be offset, pre-SBC EBITDA margin grinds down to 17.5% (IT-services margin ~14-15%), and Wipro keeps lagging TCS/Infosys under a fourth strategy reset. No solvency axis: net cash and a 70%+ payout mean the downside is a shrinking annuity, not distress, which is why the bear is not weighted higher than 30%.

scenario_narratives.base: Flat USD business carried by INR depreciation and bolt-on M&A; margin recovers part-way from the Q1 FY2027 trough; 24-25% cash tax; 15% of incremental revenue absorbed by working capital. Intrinsic value is dominated by the existing Rs118-135bn/yr owner-FCF annuity plus Rs218bn net cash, not by growth.
scenario_narratives.bull: Large-deal ramp plus consulting/AI-native pivot delivers 3-4% USD organic growth and a 21% pre-SBC EBITDA margin; INR terminal growth 4%.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI deflation of ADM pricing outruns new bookings; USD revenue shrinks 2-3%/yr to FY2030, margin erodes to 17.5%; the stock becomes a slowly shrinking high-payout annuity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house 15/50/35 to 30/50/20. Bear up because the dominant risk, AI compressing the labour-arbitrage ADM core, is structural rather than cyclical, three consecutive years of flat USD revenue show it is already biting, and the Analysis JSON grades it high severity; it is capped at 30% because there is no solvency or covenant axis (Rs218bn net cash, no net debt). Bull down to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once -- the booking-to-revenue lag closing, a margin recovery management itself says will take several quarters, and a consulting/AI pivot succeeding where three earlier strategy resets did not -- and because Wipro has lagged TCS/Infosys on both growth and margin for most of a decade.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Wipro is valued as a mature, net-cash IT-services annuity, not a growth company. The house owner-FCF basis expenses SBC (small here), charges the full lease cash cost, strips all investment income from the flows while adding the Rs396bn cash-and-investments pile (and Rs29bn non-current investments) in the bridge, and refuses to perpetuate the sub-book cash tax rate. The share count is the post-June-2026-buyback fully diluted figure held flat. Growth is modelled in INR and converted to the USD ADS at spot, so INR depreciation shows up in the flows and is offset by the INR discount rate rather than being added on top. The decision variable is the probability-weighted USD value against the USD1.72 ADS price; the 15% hurdle entry price will sit well below intrinsic value because the model discounts at 11.5% and the business grows ~3% nominal.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI-driven price deflation on application development and maintenance renewals compressing both revenue and margin faster than the bear path assumes
INR/USD: every 1% INR appreciation cuts INR revenue ~Rs2-2.5bn/quarter; the USD ADS value depends on the spot rate at which INR value is converted (a 5% INR move is a 5% move in the USD IV)
Cash tax normalisation: Rs102bn of accrued/disputed tax liabilities could crystallise as cash, and the shelter already excluded from the flows could reverse further
Capital allocation: Rs375bn of buybacks and Rs180bn of dividends in two years at a flat top line; a large-ticket acquisition at a full price would convert net cash to goodwill
Balance-sheet vintage: June-2026 cash and FY2027 flows overlap by one quarter (~Rs2.6/share), and the fx_rate is dated 2026-10-04 and does not move with refresh_price.py
